d.d: The remains of a destroyed or dilapidated construction, such as a house or castle.
The state of being a ruin, destroyed or decayed.
d.x: The monastery has fallen into ruin.

d.d: Something that leads to serious trouble or destruction.
d.x: Gambling has been the ruin of many.

d.d: To cause the fiscal ruin of; to bankrupt or drive out of business.
d.x: With all these purchases, you surely mean to ruin us!

d.d: To destroy or render something no longer usable or operable.
d.x: He ruined his new white slacks by accidentally spilling oil on them.

d.d: To destroy (e.g. a city) so as to leave ruins.
The state of being ruined, a state of devastation or destruction.
The act of ruining or wrecking.
The cause of being ruined, destroyed or lost.
